name: Haldi
traditionalUses: Sore throat gargle with salt water
Coughs and colds in warm milk
kitchenUse: Cooked into food with a little fat and black pepper, which help absorption; or a pinch in warm milk (haldi doodh).

typicalUse.note: Concentrated curcumin supplements are much stronger than kitchen turmeric.

cautions.note: Avoid medicinal amounts with gallstones or bile duct obstruction.
Stop supplements two weeks before surgery.

Liver injury has been reported with turmeric and curcumin supplements, especially products made to be highly absorbed. Stop and see a doctor if you notice tiredness, nausea, poor appetite, dark urine or yellowing of the skin or eyes.
Culinary amounts are fine; turmeric supplements may be unsafe in pregnancy.
Little is known about amounts above those in food while breastfeeding; keep to culinary use.

interactions.effect: Supplements may increase bleeding risk with blood thinners.

evidence.summary: Many human trials, especially for knee osteoarthritis pain, look promising, but higher-quality studies are needed before firm conclusions. Absorption from plain turmeric is low.
